thread:
riya (support): heads-up — we've been getting multiple customer escalations this morning about p95/p99 spikes on text-generation endpoints. they all report timeouts or responses taking 3-10s longer than usual since ~02:00 UTC.

angelo (eng-runtime): thanks, riya. which model/cluster? any commonalities?

riya (support): majority on `gpt-open-2b` hosted on eu-west-1 dedicated pools. sampling two tickets: one shows increased tail latency on long-context chat sessions, other shows sporadic 503s then slow responses. both include GPU memory pressure traces from the customer side.

sam (eng-sre): I pulled infra metrics for eu-west-1 dedicated ring. notable: node-level GPU memory usage steady, but `gpu_free_mem` fragments and our per-GPU free contiguous region drops before OOMs. p99 latency correlates with GC-like spikes on allocator logs.

mike (infra): interesting — we've seen allocator fragmentation on older CUDA releases. are we still on `cuda/11.4 + default ptmalloc` for those pools?

angelo (eng-runtime): yes — these pools were created before the allocator-tuning rollout. runtime logs show KV cache growth for long sessions: KV size per session increases with prompt history and is kept in GPU memory. combined with fragmentation that can cause allocation slowdowns (searching free lists) and some OOM fallbacks.

priya (eng-ml): customer repro indicates average context length jumped from ~512 to ~1500 tokens after a product change (they started sending full conversation). that explains heavy KV growth.

sam (eng-sre): placing quick telemetry: run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free,memory.total --format=csv -l 2` and our node logs show free memory oscillating and occasional `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` backoffs in runtime. latency > p99 when we hit those allocation retries.

angelo (eng-runtime): proposed immediate mitigations: 1) change routing to fallback to a smaller model variant for sessions with >1024 tokens; 2) enable allocator tuning flags (set `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1`, switch to `jemalloc`) on the affected pools; 3) add KV eviction policy for inactive sessions. short-term I can push 1 and 2 as config flags.

mike (infra): i can roll jemalloc on a canary node in eu-west-1 and run the same customer load. suggest we cordon one node, deploy, then re-run synthetic reproducer.

riya (support): i'll coordinate with the customer to run their session trace against the canary tomorrow at 03:30 UTC. also will ask them to share full headers so we can detect large contexts server-side.

sam (eng-sre): operational checklist for now: - cordon + drain canary node - deploy jemalloc build + `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1` - monitor p95/p99, `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` events, and allocator slow-path logs - if improved, schedule staged rollout.

angelo (eng-runtime): added a quick diagnostic endpoint to runtime to dump: `kv_entries`, `kv_total_bytes`, `num_active_sessions`, and `largest_free_block_bytes` for each GPU. sample call:

```
GET /_internal/gpu_debug?node=NODE_ID
response: {"kv_entries": 184, "kv_total_bytes": 124M, "num_active_sessions": 42, "largest_free_block_bytes": 64M}
```

priya (eng-ml): two notes: 1) model quantization differences can increase temporary allocator churn during kernel selection; 2) some model ops allocate transient workspace buffers that look like fragmentation at the OS allocator level. reducing `max_batch_size` for long-context routes might reduce transient peaks.

mike (infra): another potential quick win: enable periodic in-place defragmentation (NVMM/NVML-supported) or restart the process gracefully once fragmentation crosses threshold. but restarts cause brief requests to fallback; we should pair with routing fallback (angelo's suggestion).

riya (support): customer is ok with temporary fallbacks. they prefer reliability over perfect model fidelity. i'll request permission to switch sessions >1024 tokens to `gpt-open-1b` during the test window. :thumbsup:

angelo (eng-runtime): implementation plan: i. add route rule: if `context_len > 1024` then route to `gpt-open-1b` or optionally `gpt-open-2b-quantized`. ii. add runtime flag `allocator_profile=true` for verbose logging. iii. add `kv_eviction_idle_seconds=900` to lower memory footprint. iv. canary jemalloc on 1 node. v. monitor p95/p99 and OOM error rate.

sam (eng-sre): I'll wire up alerts to watch these signals: - anomaly on `gpu_largest_free_block_bytes` - rapid rise in `cuda_alloc_retries` - p99 latency delta > 200ms sustained for 5m - `OOM_kill` events on gpu host.

mike (infra): rolling plan: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 hours if metrics look good. rollback script prepared to revert allocator env and routing rules.

priya (eng-ml): for longer-term: 1) add KV compression for older messages (gzip or LZ4 GPU-friendly) to bound KV growth; 2) add sticky session TTLs and eviction thresholds; 3) evaluate switching heavy-context customers to dedicated reserved capacity with larger GPUs where contiguous allocation is less of an issue.

riya (support): thanks team. i'll update the affected tickets with the mitigation timeline (canary at 03:30 UTC), ask customers for repro traces, and confirm they accept temporary routing.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: jemalloc-canary -> eu-west-1/node-07 by mike at 03:25 UTC.

angelo (eng-runtime): i'll enable routing rule and `kv_eviction_idle_seconds=900` at 03:28 UTC behind the canary switch.

sam (eng-sre): after canary results we should capture a full heap profile and allocator histograms. if fragmentation persists, we may need to instrument per-GPU slab allocators and consider kernel-level defrag support.

mike (infra): canary done, running the customer's trace now. preliminary: p99 dropped from 1.8s to 700ms on canary node; `largest_free_block_bytes` stabilized. i'm collecting logs.

riya (support): customer confirms degraded incidents stopped during canary window. they asked: will this be permanent?

angelo (eng-runtime): next steps: schedule staged rollout tomorrow morning, implement KV compression PoC, and draft KB for customers about context-length best practices. i'll open follow-up tickets for long-term fixes.

riya (support): great — closing the escalation after staged rollout success. will link KB and timeline in tickets. :white_check_mark:

sam (eng-sre): nice work. leaving trace references in the incident channel.

mike (infra): note to self: add allocator tuning to infra runbook.

angelo (eng-runtime): thanks all. we'll keep monitoring.
